significance.justification: A verified-positive result would license the conclusion that model-internal brightness varies with symmetry breaking while the energy gap remains nearly fixed, that matched symmetry-preserving changes do not produce the same response, and that parity- and spin-forbidden transitions dissociate; this is a form-(iii) ordering/invariance plus the form-(ii) causal claim that an "allowedness" direction changes absorption without changing the gap. It would establish both a phenomenon and a mechanism, fixing expectations for several counterfactual transition classes rather than merely showing decodability; this matters because QM8 in MoleculeNet (Wu et al., 2018, DOI: 10.1039/C7SC02664A) operationalizes excited-state learning through targets including oscillator strengths, while the excited-state ML literature surveyed by Westermayr and Marquetand (Chemical Reviews, 2021, DOI: 10.1021/acs.chemrev.0c00749) relies heavily on predictive-property benchmarks. True and false are distinguishable, but because the hypothesis is conjunctive, a negative result would decisively reject the full selection-rule representation package for the models concerned without by itself proving the claim's stronger alternative that they use only a gap correlate. In the topic-substitution check, replacing the symmetry-at-fixed-gap and parity/spin dissociation with the generic topic question would reduce this to the median mechanism probe, so the specific multi-condition law—not the scientific domain's general importance—supports the above-median score.

reach.justification: The claim names reusable handles: the "Brightness-Beyond-Gap Index," "Symmetry-Break-vs-Preserve Causal Asymmetry," an "intensity-error failure predictor," and an "allowedness/brightness" steering direction. Its strongest use is ex ante because the proposed audit would be run "before deploying a model for dark/bright-state design," giving practitioners an opportunity to gate optical-property models or avoid using them for OLED-emitter and forbidden-transition screening. Per-model re-extraction would still be needed, and the substantive finding of whether a new model contains the mechanism would have to be re-established, but the symmetry-breaking-versus-preserving response and parity/spin dissociation provide transferable audit relations across molecular or materials models rather than only a description of one latent feature. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: a generic inquiry into scientific representations supplies no pre-deployment gate, whereas these quoted handles can be used by model auditors and photochemistry or optical-materials practitioners outside the immediate interpretability research line.
